title: Hallo! Wie heißt du?

situation.setting: Anna and Raj meet for the first time at a language course in Berlin.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.de: Hallo! Ich heiße Anna. Und du?
lines.en: Hi! My name is Anna. And you?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.en: Hi, Anna. My name is Raj.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.de: Ich komme aus Indien. Und du?
lines.en: I come from India. And you?

grammar.title: Regular verbs: ich, du, Sie
grammar.intro: German verbs have an infinitive ending in -en (heißen, kommen, wohnen). To use a verb you remove -en to get the stem, then add an ending that matches the subject. In a statement the verb always sits in the second position of the sentence.
watchOut: Sie (formal you) is always written with a capital S, and the verb takes the -en ending, like the infinitive.
heißen has du heißt, not heißst: the stem already ends in an s-sound, so the -st shortens to -t.
In W-questions the question word is first and the verb is still second: Woher kommst du?

exercises.prompt: You meet a stranger in the afternoon and want to greet them politely. What do you say?
exercises.explain: Guten Tag is the polite, all-purpose daytime greeting. Hallo is friendlier and informal.
kommen aus + country means 'to come from'.
ich takes the ending -e: ich heiße.
du takes the ending -st: du kommst.
The formal question is Wie heißen Sie? The verb ending -en matches Sie.

exercises.prompt: You meet your new boss for the first time. Which pronoun do you use?
exercises.explain: Use Sie with strangers, older people and in business settings until they offer du.
The question word comes first, the verb is second.

exercises.prompt: Match the German with the English.

culture: German has two words for 'you'. Use Sie with strangers, older people, officials and at work; use du with friends, family, children and, increasingly, among young people. If in doubt, start with Sie. Germans usually say Guten Tag until the evening, and Tschüss is a friendly, everyday way to say goodbye.
canDo: I can greet someone formally and informally.
I can say my name and ask someone theirs.
I can say where I come from and ask where someone else is from.
